question.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),\,y=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2.$ Given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t))}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =\frac{6{sec}^{2}⁡(3t)}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =2{sec}^{3}⁡(3t).\end{aligned}
$$
